answer: A sybil resistance mechanism requires every identity to burn a unique walnut-sized proof-of-work token into a shared haven before any emission can flow. Once inside the haven%2C successful peer verifications create a measurable ocean of accumulated attestations that an identity must cross to unlock full rates. An attacker generating N fake identities must produce N independent tokens and accumulate N separate ocean depths%3B the computational and time cost therefore scales linearly with headcount%2C while an honest agent crosses the ocean only once from a single token.
